drafts.title: Front seats provide extended thigh support for tall drivers and rear seats offer competitor-level legroom
drafts.description: Tall drivers must feel the front-seat cushion supports their thighs; rear passengers must have legroom at least as good as main competitors. The car should deliver both outcomes for tall-driver comfort and rear-seat competitiveness.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: User test: among drivers >= 190 cm (6'3"), at least 90% report adequate thigh support in a static comfort assessment; rear knee clearance (seatback to front-seat cushion) must be greater than or equal to the average knee clearance of the top 3 competitor models measured by the OEM test method.
assumptions: Competitor knee-clearance data (top 3 rivals in the segment) is available at development time and measured with identical fixture/seat settings.
Tall-driver (>=190 cm) panel is representative; 'adequate' is based on a validated 5-point comfort scale where >=4 is acceptable.
uncertainties: Exact competitor benchmarks may change before launch; packaging trade-offs with electrified powertrain variants could affect rear knee room.

drafts.title: Cup holders fit common bottle and travel-mug sizes without interference
drafts.description: Customers must be able to store commonly used bottles and travel mugs in the cup holders (center console) without forcing or blocking adjacent controls or armrest movement.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Fit test: cup holders must hold simultaneously (a) a 1.0 L bottle up to 90 mm diameter and (b) a 500 ml travel mug up to 85 mm diameter in their intended positions, with successful insertion/removal in at least 95% of 20 common-bottle samples.
assumptions: Common bottle sample set reflects US market sizes (1.0 L bottles, 750 ml, 500 ml travel mugs, 20 popular models).
uncertainties: Aftermarket bottle geometries vary; extreme insulated mugs (>90 mm diameter) may still not fit.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably and quickly on first attempt
drafts.description: Hands-free tailgate gesture must operate consistently when the customer performs the standard foot gesture and must not require multiple attempts under normal use conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Operational test: tailgate opens within 2 seconds of a valid foot gesture on the first attempt in at least 95% of trials across 100 test cycles including varied footwear and wet/dirty ground conditions.
assumptions: Standardized foot-gesture test protocol is defined (distance, foot motion) and repeatable across test operators.
Environmental conditions include dry, wet, and light debris scenarios representative of customer use.
uncertainties: Extreme snow/ice or heavy soiling scenarios may still reduce detection reliability; hardware placement changes may be required.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting offers a much larger color palette and fine brightness control
drafts.description: Customers must be able to personalize interior ambient lighting with many colors and fine-grained brightness to match preferences and moods.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: System supports at least 64 distinct hues and continuous brightness control from 0–100% (user-adjustable slider) with at least 10 named preset scenes; in a preference test, 90% of customers can find a desired color/scene within 30 seconds.
assumptions: Lighting hardware and software will allow selection of 64 distinct hues and continuous brightness control at the time of successor development.
Preference test panel reflects target customer demographics.
uncertainties: Legal constraints on external/exterior lighting colors are out of scope; interior electrical budget may limit absolute brightness.

drafts.title: Seat memory restores saved positions reliably on first command
drafts.description: When a driver selects a saved seat memory position, the seat (and linked steering/mirror presets) must reach the saved configuration reliably without repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Functional reliability: first-command restoration success rate of at least 98% measured over 100 consecutive memory recalls across temperature and battery states; successful restores must be within driver-acceptable fit (driver-rated acceptable on a 5-point scale) in at least 95% of cases.
assumptions: Test includes variations in ambient temperature and vehicle battery state representative of customer conditions.
Driver-acceptable fit is validated with the same panel used for other seating tests.
uncertainties: Interactions with aftermarket seat adjustments or manual overrides could affect reliability in field use.

drafts.title: Flush door handles operate reliably in freezing conditions
drafts.description: Customers must be able to open the vehicle from outside even after freezing weather and light icing without recurring manual unfreezing steps.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cold-weather test: flush door handles operate successfully in 99% of attempts after exposure to -25°C for 24 hours and after a light ice accumulation cycle (as defined by test protocol) across 200 door-actuation trials.
assumptions: Cold-climate test protocols match industry standards for ice/icing simulation.
Customer expectation is single-action entry without manual defrosting or prying.
uncertainties: Extreme ice conditions beyond test protocol or heavy salt/contaminant build-up may still impair operation.

drafts.title: Trunk includes a power outlet able to run a typical cooler box
drafts.description: Customers can power a portable cooler from the trunk without needing aftermarket adapters or running cable to the cabin.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A dedicated trunk power outlet is provided and able to continuously supply at least 40 W (approx. 3.3 A at 12 V) for 4 hours; outlet location is accessible and labeled for customer use.
assumptions: 40 W is representative of typical portable cooler power draw for customer use cases.
Safety and circuit protection for trunk outlet will meet vehicle electrical system requirements.
uncertainties: Higher-draw coolers (>40 W) will require different solutions; availability of accessory inverters is not assumed.

drafts.title: Front-end design to meet EU pedestrian protection regulation (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the front end complies with the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: front-end must meet the applicable EU pedestrian protection regulation requirements at homologation.
assumptions: Regulation text and test procedures will be available and final at the time of vehicle homologation.
uncertainties: Design solutions to meet the regulation may conflict with styling or other packaging targets.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance request – out of scope for customer-facing successor requirements; this is a homologation/engineering specification.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbags FMVSS 208 certification (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: rear-seat airbag system must meet FMVSS 208 certification when sold in markets requiring it.
assumptions: Certification path and test requirements are defined by the regulator and will be followed by engineering.
uncertainties: Certification may require design changes that affect interior packaging.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/certification request – out of scope for customer-facing successor requirements; engineering/homologation task.

drafts.title: Headlight beam pattern to follow ECE R112 where required (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that headlight beam patterns conform to ECE R112 rules in every market.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: headlight beam patterns meet ECE R112 requirements in markets where ECE rules apply at homologation.
assumptions: Market-specific homologation requirements will be followed; beam pattern configurations may vary by market.
uncertainties: Global harmonization of beam patterns may not be achievable without market-specific hardware/configuration.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/homologation requirement – not a customer-facing successor feature.

drafts.title: Volume knob encoder specification (engineering spec request)
drafts.description: Customers requested the volume knob use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: volume control encoder specified as a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder per customer ask.
assumptions: Encoder type is an engineering implementation detail; customer outcome (ease of use) should be translated to a user-facing requirement if retention is desired.
uncertainties: Alternative technologies may produce equivalent customer experience without the specific encoder.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component/part request – engineering specification, out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Side-window glass thickness specification (engineering spec request)
drafts.description: Customers requested 4.5 mm thick laminated glass for the side windows.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: side windows specified as 4.5 mm laminated glass per customer input.
assumptions: Glass thickness request is a materials/engineering specification; sound and safety performance should be expressed as customer-facing outcomes instead.
uncertainties: Weight, cost, and acoustic trade-offs may make this exact thickness infeasible across all variants.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific material/component specification – engineering scope, not a customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Seat-foam density specification (engineering spec request)
drafts.description: Customers requested seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: seat cushion foam density specified as 55 kg/m³ per customer input.
assumptions: Foam density is an engineering/material parameter; equivalent or better subjective comfort can be achieved by multiple material solutions.
uncertainties: Exact density may vary by trim/variant to balance comfort, durability and cost.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific material/component specification – engineering scope, not a customer-facing requirement.

drafts.title: Residual value guarantee request (business request)
drafts.description: Customers ask BMW to guarantee a residual value of 60% after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: guarantee of 60% residual value after 5 years as stated by customer feedback.
assumptions: Residual value guarantees are a commercial/financial decision requiring legal/financial frameworks.
uncertainties: Market conditions and variant mix will affect realizable residual values; this is outside product design scope.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/financial request – out of scope for vehicle product requirements.

drafts.title: Production-cost reduction request (business/engineering request)
drafts.description: Customers ask BMW to cut production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request: reduce production cost per car by 8% relative to current baseline.
assumptions: Production-cost targets are internal business objectives requiring cross-functional programs.
uncertainties: Cost reductions may affect perceived quality if not carefully managed; this is not a direct customer-facing requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/production cost target – outside the scope of customer-facing successor requirements.
